analytics.deepDiveComplianceInfo: Three health checks of the cooperative: how much of its assets belongs to members, how much is held as cash and bank balances, and how much of the loan book is more than 90 days late. A gauge that cannot be computed is left out instead of showing zero. Taken from the approved financial statement. Formulas: equity divided by assets, liquid assets divided by assets, and non-performing loans divided by gross loans.
analytics.deepDiveTrendInfo: How the main balances of the cooperative move from month to month. It helps spot growth or decline early. Taken from approved financial statements, in USD, at each month's end.
analytics.noHistoricalTrendData: No historical trend data available yet
analytics.deepDiveProvisioningInfo: How much of the loan book is more than 30 days late and how much of that is covered by provisions. The uncovered part is money the cooperative could lose. Taken from the approved financial statement at the period end. Formulas: overdue amount is gross loans times PAR over 30 days; covered amount is that overdue amount times provision coverage; at risk is overdue minus covered.
analytics.deepDiveMembershipInfo: Who the members are: the split by gender and how many are active or dormant. It shows how balanced and engaged the membership is. Taken from the uploaded member ledger of the approved submission. Formula: members in each group divided by all members, as a percentage.
analytics.deepDiveLiquidityInfo: How concentrated the fixed deposits are. If a few deposits or short terms make up most of the money, members withdrawing at once could strain the cooperative. Taken from the uploaded fixed deposit ledger. Formula: deposits that depend on a single depositor divided by all fixed deposits, as a percentage.
analytics.deepDiveEngagementInfo: How much members take part in running the cooperative, for example by attending the Annual General Meeting. Higher means stronger member control. Taken from the attendance and voting flags in the uploaded member ledger. Formula: members who attended divided by all members, as a percentage.
analytics.deepDiveInclusionInfo: How much of the credit goes to women, young people and rural borrowers. It shows whether lending reaches the groups the cooperative aims to serve. Taken from the borrower flags in the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: loans to each group divided by active loans, as a percentage.
analytics.deepDiveAgriInfo: How well equipped the cooperative is for farming: storage, processing, irrigation and use of shared inputs. It shows resilience to weather and market shocks. Taken from the farm cooperative ledger of the approved submission. Formula: cooperatives or farmers with each asset divided by all recorded, as a percentage.
analytics.concentrationDesc: Percentage of total term deposits held by the top 5% of members. A high number implies liquidity risk.
analytics.financialIndicatorsSubtitle: Supervisory Audits, Financial Ratios & Performance Indicators ({{year}})
analytics.financialRatiosMappingsDesc: This dashboard aggregates key prudential and efficiency ratios:
analytics.ratiosCarInfo: How much of the assets belongs to members rather than creditors. Higher means a stronger cushion against losses. Formula: total equity divided by total assets, as a percentage.
analytics.ratiosDelinquencyInfo: How much of the loan book is late. Lower is better. Formula: non-performing loans (over 90 days late) divided by gross loans, and PAR over 30 days as loans over 30 days late divided by gross loans.
analytics.ratiosRoaRoeInfo: How much surplus the cooperative makes compared with its assets and with members' equity. Higher is better. Formula: net surplus divided by total assets, and net surplus divided by total equity, for the period covered and not annualised.
analytics.ratiosOperatingEfficiencyInfo: How much the running costs weigh against the size of the cooperative and against its interest margin. Lower is leaner. Formula: operating expenses divided by total assets, and operating expenses divided by financial income minus financial expenses.
analytics.indicatorCarEqAssets: Capital Adequacy Ratio: Total Equity / Total Assets
analytics.indicatorAssetStructure: ASSET STRUCTURE & QUALITY (ESTRUCTURA Y CALIDAD DE ACTIVOS)
analytics.indicatorProductiveDelinquency: Arrears up to 90 days / Gross Loans
analytics.indicatorOpexRatio: Operating Expense Ratio: Operating Expenses / Total Assets
analytics.indicatorLiquidFunds: Liquid Funds Ratio: Liquid Assets / Total Assets
analytics.genderParticipationTooltip: The share of members who are women, men or another gender. It shows how well the membership is balanced. Taken from the gender recorded in the uploaded member ledger of the approved submission; members without a recorded gender are left out of the percentages. Formula: members of each gender divided by all members, as a percentage.
analytics.genderParticipationNoData: No membership gender data recorded for this period.
analytics.netTotalCooperativesTooltip: The number of cooperatives that have an approved return for the selected period, out of all cooperatives in view. It shows how complete the picture is. Counts approved submissions only.
analytics.netTotalMembersTooltip: The number of members recorded in the member registers of the cooperatives in view, including dormant and exited members. Taken from the uploaded member ledger of approved submissions. Formula: all members in the register.
analytics.netTotalSavingsTooltip: The sum of every balance in the uploaded member savings register. It comes from the member ledger, not from the balance sheet, so it can differ from member savings on the financial statement. Converted to USD at each submission's frozen rate. Formula: sum of all savings account balances.
analytics.netTotalLoansTooltip: The outstanding balance of the loans in the uploaded loan book, without written-off loans. It comes from the member ledger, not from the balance sheet, so it can differ from gross loans on the financial statement. Converted to USD. Formula: sum of balances of loans that are not written off.
analytics.netFixedDepositsTooltip: The sum of the fixed deposits in the uploaded fixed deposit register. It comes from the member ledger, not from the balance sheet. Converted to USD at each submission's frozen rate. Formula: sum of fixed deposit balances.
analytics.netOnTimeRepaymentTooltip: The share of loans repaid on schedule across the network. Higher is better. Taken from the repayment regularity in the loan ledgers (or from performing status when regularity is not recorded), combined across cooperatives by weighting with their number of active loans. Formula: loans repaid on time divided by active loans, as a percentage.
analytics.netTotalApexesTooltip: Total number of active apex organizations within the federation.
analytics.netTotalMembersTooltip2: The number of members recorded in the member register, including dormant and exited members. It shows the size of the membership base. Taken from the uploaded member ledger of the approved submission. Formula: all members in the register.
analytics.netActiveMembersTooltip: Members whose status in the register is active. A high share means an engaged membership. Taken from the uploaded member ledger of the approved submission. Formula: members with status active.
analytics.netDormantMembersTooltip: Members whose status in the register is dormant, meaning they are still members but no longer take part. A high share suggests members need to be re-engaged. Taken from the uploaded member ledger. Formula: members with status dormant.
analytics.netYouthMembersTooltip: Members aged 35 or younger. It shows how well the cooperative reaches young people. Taken from the age group of each member in the uploaded member ledger. Formula: members under 18 plus members aged 18 to 35.
analytics.netSavingsAccountsTooltip: The number of savings accounts recorded in the savings register. It shows how widely savings are used. Taken from the uploaded savings ledger of the approved submission. Formula: all savings accounts in the register.
analytics.netTotalSavingsTooltip2: The sum of every balance in the uploaded savings register. It comes from the member ledger, not from the balance sheet, so it can differ from the savings on the financial statement. Shown in USD. Formula: sum of all savings account balances.
analytics.netActiveSaversTooltip: The number of savings accounts whose status is active. The figure counts accounts, not people, so one member with two accounts counts twice. Taken from the uploaded savings ledger. Formula: savings accounts with status active.
analytics.netRegularSaversTooltip: The share of savings accounts that receive regular contributions, monthly or quarterly. It shows whether members save steadily. Taken from the contribution frequency in the uploaded savings ledger. Formula: accounts with monthly or quarterly contributions divided by all savings accounts, as a percentage.
analytics.netLoanAccountsTooltip: The number of loans recorded in the loan register, with the number still active shown beneath. It shows how many members borrow. Taken from the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: all loans in the register; active means not written off.
analytics.netTotalLoansTooltip2: The outstanding balance of the loans in the uploaded loan register, without written-off loans. It comes from the member ledger, not from the balance sheet. Shown in USD. Formula: sum of balances of loans that are not written off.
analytics.netLoansInArrearsTooltip: The number of loans whose status in the loan register is in arrears, meaning repayments are late. It differs from PAR, which measures the money value overdue in the financial statement. Taken from the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: loans with status arrears.
analytics.netOnTimeRepaymentTooltip2: The share of active loans repaid on schedule. Higher is better. Taken from the repayment regularity in the loan ledger, or from performing status when regularity is not recorded. Formula: loans repaid on time divided by active loans, as a percentage.
analytics.netFdAccountsTooltip: The number of fixed deposits recorded in the fixed deposit register, with the number still active shown beneath. Taken from the uploaded fixed deposit ledger. Formula: all fixed deposits in the register.
analytics.netTotalFdBalanceTooltip: The sum of the balances of all fixed deposits in the register. It comes from the member ledger, not from the balance sheet. Shown in USD. Formula: sum of fixed deposit balances.
analytics.netFdPenetrationTooltip: The share of members who hold a fixed deposit. It shows how far this product reaches the membership. Taken from the fixed deposit and member ledgers, and for a network it is worked out from total members, not from an average of cooperative percentages. Formula: members with a fixed deposit divided by total members, as a percentage.
analytics.netRolloverRateTooltip: Of the fixed deposits that reached maturity, the share the member chose to renew. A high value shows members trust the cooperative with their money. Taken from the fixed deposit ledger. Formula: rolled over deposits divided by matured plus rolled over deposits, as a percentage.
analytics.netSavingsPortfolioHealthInfo: Three signs of how healthy savings are: how many members save, how many accounts get regular contributions and how many accounts are active. Higher is better. Taken from the uploaded savings and member ledgers. Formulas: members with savings divided by members, accounts with monthly or quarterly contributions divided by accounts, and active accounts divided by accounts, as percentages.
analytics.netLoanPortfolioBreakdownSub: Performing vs. arrears across the network
analytics.netLoanPortfolioBreakdownInfo: The number and value of loans: all loans, those still active, those in arrears and those restructured, and the amount lent against the amount still owed. It shows the size and quality of lending. Taken from the uploaded loan ledgers, in USD thousands. Written-off loans are not counted as active or outstanding.
analytics.netLiquidityRiskInfo: How concentrated the fixed deposits are across the network. If a few deposits or short terms make up most of the money, withdrawals at once could strain the cooperatives. Taken from the uploaded fixed deposit ledgers. Formula: deposits that depend on a single depositor divided by all fixed deposits, as a percentage.
analytics.netGovernanceInfo: How much members take part in running the network, for example by attending the Annual General Meeting. Higher means stronger member control. Taken from the attendance and voting flags in the uploaded member ledgers. Formula: members who attended divided by all members, as a percentage.
analytics.netInclusionInfo: How much of the credit goes to women, young people and rural borrowers across the network. It shows whether lending reaches the groups it aims to serve. Taken from the borrower flags in the uploaded loan ledgers. Formula: loans to each group divided by active loans, as a percentage.
analytics.netDemographicsInfo: Who the members are across the network: the split by gender and how many are active, dormant or exited. It shows how balanced and engaged the membership is. Taken from the uploaded member ledgers. Formula: members in each group divided by all members, as a percentage.
analytics.netAgeGeographySub: Member age distribution and geographic spread
analytics.netAgeGeographyInfo: How members are spread by age and by place of living, urban or rural. It shows whether the membership is young and whether it reaches the countryside. Taken from the age group and area recorded in the uploaded member ledgers. The age groups are under 18, 18 to 35, 36 to 50 and over 50, which differ from the bands of the questionnaire dashboard.
analytics.spreadsheetAccountMappingDesc: The cooperative's raw credit portfolio is mapped to the standard chart of accounts:
analytics.pcTotalArrearsCode: Sum of account codes 1202 (1-30 days), 1203 (31-60 days), and 1204 (61-90 days).
analytics.pcTotalNonPerformingCode: Mapped to account code 1205 (non-performing loans > 90 days).
analytics.pcNote: Note: Product-specific subcategories (Productive, Consumption, Microcredit, etc.) are consolidated into the main category totals in the standard chart of accounts.
analytics.portfolioOverviewTooltip: The overall size of the cooperative month by month. It shows how the balance sheet grows or shrinks. Taken from approved financial statements, in USD, at each month's end. Total assets already include the loans and liquid assets shown in the other charts, so they are not added to them. Formula: total assets (1999).
analytics.savingsLoansDepositsTooltip: Three balance-sheet amounts month by month: liquid assets, gross loans and member savings. The line shows whether cash and loans exceed savings. Taken from approved financial statements, in USD, at each month's end. The bars are separate figures and are not meant to add up to total assets. Formula for the line: liquid assets plus gross loans minus member savings (1100 plus 1200 minus 2100).
analytics.totalSavingsBalanceNote: From the uploaded savings register, not the balance sheet
analytics.loadErrorDesc: Something went wrong while loading the benchmark. Please try again.

headline.totalAssetsTooltip: Everything the cooperatives in view own. It shows the overall size of the network. Taken from approved financial statements at the latest month reported, converted to USD at each submission's frozen rate. Formula: total assets (1999).
headline.equityToAssetsTooltip: How much of the assets belongs to members rather than to creditors. Higher is safer; negative means debts exceed assets. Taken from approved statements at the latest month reported. Formula: total equity divided by total assets, as a percentage (3999 over 1999).

analytics.watchListEmpty: Not enough cooperatives to build a watch list.

tip.totalIncome: All the money earned by the cooperatives in the period, mainly loan interest and fees. It is the top line of profitability. Taken from approved financial statements and added up over the months reported, in USD. Formula: total income (4999) summed over the months reported.
tip.totalExpenditure: All the money spent to run the cooperatives in the period, including interest paid, staff and administration. Lower is better for the same income. Taken from approved financial statements and added up over the months reported, in USD. Formula: total expenses (5999) summed over the months reported.
tip.netIncome: What is left after all expenses. A positive value is a surplus, a negative value a loss. Taken from approved financial statements over the months reported, in USD. Formula: net surplus (6999) as reported, otherwise total income minus total expenses.
tip.roa: How much surplus is made for each unit of assets. Higher means assets are used more profitably. Taken from approved statements, for the period covered and not annualised, so a quarter reads lower than a year. Formula: net income divided by total assets, as a percentage.
tip.roe: How much surplus is made for each unit of members' equity. Higher means members' capital works harder. Taken from approved statements, for the period covered and not annualised. Formula: net income divided by total equity, as a percentage.
tip.expensesToIncome: How much of every unit earned goes on expenses. Below 100 percent means a surplus; lower is better. Taken from approved statements over the months reported. Formula: total expenses divided by total income, as a percentage.
tip.selfSufficiency: Whether income covers costs. Above 100 percent the cooperatives cover their costs from their own income; higher is better. Taken from approved statements over the months reported. Formula: total income divided by total expenses, as a percentage.
tip.netInterestMargin: What the cooperatives earn from lending and investing after paying interest to savers and lenders, compared with their size. Higher is better. Taken from approved statements, for the period covered and not annualised. Formula: financial income (4100) minus financial expenses (5100), divided by total assets, as a percentage.
tip.grossLoans: The total amount members owe on loans, including overdue loans, before provisions. It is the main earning asset. Taken from approved financial statements at the period end, in USD. Formula: loans and advances (1200).
tip.netLoans: The loan book after setting aside money for expected losses. It is a more prudent view of what will really be recovered. Taken from approved statements at the period end, in USD. Formula: gross loans minus the allowance for loan losses (1250).
tip.par30: Portfolio at risk over 30 days: the share of the loan book that is more than 30 days late. A high value means many loans may not be repaid, so lower is better. Loans only 1 to 30 days late are not counted. Taken from approved statements at the period end. Formula: loans overdue more than 30 days divided by gross loans, as a percentage (1203, 1204, 1205 over 1200).
tip.par60: The share of the loan book that is more than 60 days late. It is a more serious warning than the 30 day measure; lower is better. Taken from approved statements at the period end. Formula: loans overdue more than 60 days divided by gross loans, as a percentage (1204, 1205 over 1200).
tip.par90: The share of the loan book that is non-performing, more than 90 days late. These loans are unlikely to be recovered; lower is better. Taken from approved statements at the period end. Formula: non-performing loans divided by gross loans, as a percentage (1205 over 1200).
tip.valueAtRisk: The money value of loans that are more than 30 days late. It is the amount behind the PAR over 30 days figure. Taken from approved statements at the period end, in USD. Formula: loans overdue more than 30 days (1203 plus 1204 plus 1205).
tip.provisions: Money set aside to absorb expected loan losses. It protects members' savings if borrowers do not repay. Taken from approved statements at the period end, shown as a positive amount in USD. Formula: allowance for loan losses (1250), general plus specific.
tip.provisionCoverage: How much of the seriously late loans is covered by provisions. Around 100 percent or more means expected losses are fully set aside; higher is safer. Taken from approved statements at the period end. Formula: provisions divided by loans overdue more than 30 days, as a percentage.
tip.liquidAssets: Cash and bank balances that can quickly be used to pay members. It shows the ability to meet withdrawals. Taken from approved statements at the period end, in USD. Formula: liquid assets (1100), which are cash, bank and short-term investments.
tip.liquidityToSavings: How much of members' savings could be repaid at once from liquid assets. The regulatory minimum is 15 percent, so higher is safer. Taken from approved statements at the period end. Formula: liquid assets divided by member savings, as a percentage (1100 over 2100).
tip.liquidityGap: How far liquidity is from the 15 percent minimum. Zero or negative means the minimum is met; a positive value is a shortfall. Formula: 15 percent minus the liquidity ratio, in percentage points.
tip.totalAssets: Everything the cooperatives own. It shows their overall size. Taken from approved financial statements at the period end, in USD. Formula: total assets (1999), which are liquid assets plus gross loans less provisions plus other assets.
tip.earningAssetRatio: The share of assets that are lent out or held as liquid funds rather than tied up in buildings and equipment. Higher means more of the money is available for members. Taken from approved statements at the period end. Formula: gross loans plus liquid assets, divided by total assets, as a percentage.
tip.memberSavingsRatio: The share of assets funded by member savings. A high share means the cooperatives rely mostly on their own members' money. Taken from approved statements at the period end. Formula: member savings divided by total assets, as a percentage (2100 over 1999).
tip.memberShareRatio: The share of assets funded by the shares members have bought. It shows how much members own directly. Taken from approved statements at the period end. Formula: member shares divided by total assets, as a percentage (3100 over 1999).
tip.borrowedFundsRatio: The share of assets funded by money borrowed from outside lenders. A high share means more dependence on lenders and more risk. Taken from approved statements at the period end. Formula: borrowings divided by total assets, as a percentage (2200 over 1999).
tip.loansToSavings: How much has been lent for each unit saved by members. Around 100 percent or more means savings are fully lent out, leaving less cash for withdrawals. Taken from approved statements at the period end. Formula: gross loans divided by member savings, as a percentage (1200 over 2100).
tip.institutionalCapital: The cooperatives' own reserves built up over time, which absorb losses. It excludes the shares members bought. Taken from approved statements at the period end, in USD. Formula: reserves (3200) plus retained earnings (3300).
tip.institutionalCapitalToAssets: How much of the assets is backed by the cooperatives' own reserves. The regulatory minimum is 8 percent; higher means a stronger cushion against losses. Taken from approved statements at the period end. Formula: institutional capital divided by total assets, as a percentage.
tip.capitalExcess: How far the institutional capital ratio is above or below the 8 percent minimum. Positive means the minimum is exceeded; negative is a deficiency. Formula: institutional capital ratio minus 8 percent, in percentage points.
tip.totalEquity: What is left for members after all debts are paid: shares, reserves and retained earnings. It shows net worth. Taken from approved statements at the period end, in USD. Formula: total equity (3999).
tip.shareCapital: The money members paid in by buying shares. It is their direct stake in the cooperatives. Taken from approved statements at the period end, in USD. Formula: member shares (3100).
tip.retainedEarnings: Surpluses kept in the cooperatives from past years instead of being paid out. They build the cooperatives' own strength. Taken from approved statements at the period end, in USD. Formula: retained earnings (3300).
tip.statutoryReserve: Reserves that must be set aside by law or by the rules of the cooperative to protect against losses. Taken from approved statements at the period end, in USD. Formula: statutory reserve (3201).

ledger.womenBorrowersTip: The share of active loans held by women. It shows whether women have fair access to credit. Taken from the borrower flag in the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: loans to women divided by active loans, as a percentage.
ledger.youthBorrowersTip: The share of active loans held by young borrowers. It shows whether young people can get credit. Taken from the youth borrower flag in the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: loans to youth borrowers divided by active loans, as a percentage.
ledger.ruralBorrowersTip: The share of active loans held by borrowers living in rural areas. It shows whether credit reaches the countryside. Taken from the rural flag in the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: loans to rural borrowers divided by active loans, as a percentage.
ledger.restructuredLoansTip: The share of loans whose repayment terms were changed because the borrower struggled to pay. A high share can hide weak loans. Taken from the loan status in the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: restructured loans divided by all loans, as a percentage.
ledger.writtenOffLoansTip: The number of loans the cooperative has given up collecting. It shows past credit losses. Taken from the loan status in the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: loans with status written off.
ledger.dormantSavingsTip: The share of savings accounts that are dormant, meaning unused. A high share means many members are not engaged. Taken from the account status in the uploaded savings ledger. Formula: dormant accounts divided by all savings accounts, as a percentage.
ledger.zeroBalanceTip: The share of savings accounts that hold no money. It shows accounts opened but not used. Taken from the zero balance flag in the uploaded savings ledger. Formula: accounts with a zero balance divided by all savings accounts, as a percentage.
ledger.averageSavingsTip: The typical amount held per savings account. It shows how deep savings are. Taken from the uploaded savings ledger, in USD. Formula: total savings balance divided by the number of savings accounts.
ledger.earlyFdWithdrawalTip: The share of fixed deposits taken out before their end date. A high share means members did not keep their money locked in as planned. Taken from the early withdrawal flag in the uploaded fixed deposit ledger. Formula: early withdrawals divided by all fixed deposits, as a percentage.

analytics.rankingSharesInfo: Each cooperative's share of the network total for the account and month chosen above. It shows which cooperatives carry the most weight. Taken from approved financial statements in USD; a cooperative with no figure for that month shows a dash and is left out of the shares. Formula: the cooperative's value divided by the sum of all values shown, as a percentage.
analytics.rankingChartInfo: Cooperatives ranked from the largest to the smallest for the account and month chosen above. It shows how concentrated the sector is. Taken from approved financial statements in USD, at each submission's frozen exchange rate. Only cooperatives with a figure for that month appear. Balance sheet accounts show the balance at that month end; the latest reported month uses each cooperative's most recent month.
analytics.pcGridInfo: Each cooperative's loan book split by repayment status: performing, in arrears, non-performing, then provisions and the net portfolio. It shows where credit risk sits. Taken from approved financial statements at the month chosen, in USD. Rows by loan purpose or days past due are not on a standard balance sheet and read n/r, not reported. Formula: net portfolio is gross loans minus provisions.
analytics.incomeGridInfo: Each cooperative's income statement side by side: what it earned, what it spent and the surplus. Balance-sheet-only statements show n/r or a dash, never a made-up zero. Taken from approved financial statements in USD, added up from January to the month chosen. Formula: net surplus equals total revenues minus interest and operating expenses and credit loss provisions.
analytics.indicatorsGridInfo: Key health ratios of each cooperative: capital, asset quality, late loans, provisions, efficiency, profitability and liquidity. They let you compare cooperatives of different sizes. Every ratio is computed from the approved financial statement at the month chosen; profitability ratios use income from January to that month, are not annualised, and show a dash when the statement has no income lines. Each row names its formula.

gridTip.calculated: A total worked out from the other rows of this grid. It uses approved financial statement figures in USD at the month chosen. Formula: see the account codes in the rows above it.
gridTip.notReportedLoans: Not reported. The financial statement does not split the loan book by loan purpose and days past due, so no figure is shown instead of a made-up zero.
gridTip.notReportedSection: A section heading. The figures are on the rows below and in the totals.
gridTip.source: Approved financial statement, account code {{codes}}, at the month chosen and in USD. Formula: the value of that account.

indicatorTip.car: How much of the assets belongs to members rather than creditors. Higher means a stronger cushion against losses. Approved statement at the month chosen. Formula: total equity divided by total assets, as a percentage.
indicatorTip.earning: The share of assets that is lent out as loans. Higher means more of the assets are working. Approved statement at the month chosen. Formula: gross loans divided by total assets, as a percentage.
indicatorTip.earningLiab: How much has been lent for each unit of member savings. Around 100 percent or more means savings are fully lent. Approved statement at the month chosen. Formula: gross loans divided by member savings, as a percentage.
indicatorTip.npl: The share of the loan book that is non-performing, more than 90 days late. Lower is better. Approved statement at the month chosen. Formula: non-performing loans divided by gross loans, as a percentage (1205 over 1200).
indicatorTip.par30: The share of the loan book that is more than 30 days late. Lower is better; loans 1 to 30 days late are not counted. Approved statement at the month chosen. Formula: loans overdue more than 30 days divided by gross loans, as a percentage (1203, 1204, 1205 over 1200).
indicatorTip.early: The share of the loan book that is 1 to 90 days late, before loans become non-performing. It is an early warning sign. Approved statement at the month chosen. Formula: loans in arrears up to 90 days divided by gross loans, as a percentage (1202, 1203, 1204 over 1200).
indicatorTip.coverage: How much of the seriously late loans is covered by provisions. Around 100 percent or more is fully covered; higher is safer. Approved statement at the month chosen. Formula: provisions divided by loans overdue more than 30 days, as a percentage.
indicatorTip.opex: The running costs of the cooperative compared with its size. Lower means a leaner operation. Approved statement, with expenses added from January to the month chosen, not annualised. A dash means no income lines were reported. Formula: operating expenses divided by total assets, as a percentage (5201 to 5204 over 1999).
indicatorTip.opexMargin: How much of the interest margin is used up by running costs. Below 100 percent the margin covers the costs; lower is better. Approved statement, added from January to the month chosen. A dash means the margin is zero or negative, or no income was reported. Formula: operating expenses divided by financial income minus financial expenses, as a percentage.
indicatorTip.roa: How much surplus is made for each unit of assets. Higher is better. Approved statement, with income added from January to the month chosen, not annualised. A dash means no income lines were reported. Formula: net surplus divided by total assets, as a percentage.
indicatorTip.roe: How much surplus is made for each unit of members' equity. Higher is better. Approved statement, with income added from January to the month chosen, not annualised. A dash means no income lines were reported. Formula: net surplus divided by total equity, as a percentage.
indicatorTip.oss: Whether income covers costs. Above 100 percent the cooperative covers its costs from its own income; higher is better. Approved statement, added from January to the month chosen. A dash means no income lines were reported. Formula: total income divided by total expenses, as a percentage.
indicatorTip.liquid: The share of assets held as cash and bank balances. It shows how much is available at short notice. Approved statement at the month chosen. Formula: liquid assets divided by total assets, as a percentage (1100 over 1999).
indicatorTip.loansDeposits: How much has been lent for each unit of member savings. Around 100 percent or more means savings are fully lent, leaving less cash for withdrawals. Approved statement at the month chosen. Formula: gross loans divided by member savings, as a percentage (1200 over 2100).

TOTAL_MISMATCH.what: The sum of the sub-category line items does not add up to the reported total. This usually means some line items were mapped to the wrong account code, or key accounts are missing.
TOTAL_MISMATCH.fix: Check each line item in the table. Look for rows with 'Low' confidence — they are likely mapped to the wrong code. Use the account code dropdown to reassign them correctly. After fixing, click Re-validate.

BALANCE_UNBALANCED.what: Total Assets ≠ Total Liabilities + Total Equity. The fundamental accounting equation is broken.
BALANCE_UNBALANCED.fix: This usually means one or more totals are mapped incorrectly. Verify that code 1999 holds Total Assets, 2999 holds Total Liabilities, and 3999 holds Total Equity. Reassign any misplaced items.

MISSING_ACCOUNT.what: A required account code is missing from the extracted data. The AI could not find or confidently map this field from your document.
MISSING_ACCOUNT.fix: Scroll to the 'Unmapped Items' section at the bottom of the table. Find the item that corresponds to this account and use the 'Assign ↑' dropdown to assign the correct code.

LIQUIDITY_CRISIS.what: Liquid assets (cash + short-term investments) cover less than 50% of short-term liabilities. This is a critical risk indicator.
LIQUIDITY_CRISIS.fix: Verify that liquid asset codes (1101, 1102, 1103, 1104) and deposit codes (2101, 2102, 2103) are correctly assigned. If the values look right, this is a genuine financial risk requiring management attention.

LOW_LIQUIDITY.what: Liquid assets are below 10% of total assets. Either cash/investments are underreported or the cooperative has very little liquid resources.
LOW_LIQUIDITY.fix: Check that all cash accounts (1101, 1102, 1103) and short-term investments (1104) have been correctly identified and mapped. Look for any cash items in the unmapped section.

CASH_TOO_LOW.what: Cash on hand and at bank is below 2% of total assets, which is dangerously low for daily operations.
CASH_TOO_LOW.fix: Verify codes 1101 (Cash on Hand), 1102 (Cash at Bank Current), 1103 (Cash at Bank Savings) are correctly mapped with the right values.

NPL_HIGH.what: Non-performing loans exceed 10% of the total loan portfolio. This is above the alert threshold.
NPL_HIGH.fix: Verify codes 1201–1205 are correctly assigned to the right loan quality buckets. If the data is correct, this reflects a real credit risk requiring management action.

UNDER_PROVISIONING.what: The specific loan loss provision (code 1252) covers less than 50% of non-performing loans (code 1205). This may be a regulatory violation.
UNDER_PROVISIONING.fix: Check that 1252 (Specific Loan Loss Provision) is mapped and stored as a NEGATIVE number. Also verify 1205 (Non-Performing Loans) is correct.

LOW_EQUITY.what: Equity is below 10% of total assets. The cooperative may be under-capitalised.
LOW_EQUITY.fix: Verify that all equity components are mapped: 3101 (Permanent Share Capital), 3102 (Withdrawable Shares), 3201 (Statutory Reserve), 3301 (Accumulated Surplus), 3302 (Current Year Surplus).

STATUTORY_RESERVE_MISSING.what: The statutory reserve (code 3201) is zero or missing. This is legally required for cooperatives.
STATUTORY_RESERVE_MISSING.fix: Check if the uploaded document includes a statutory or legal reserve. If it does, find it in the unmapped items and assign code 3201.

HIGH_LEVERAGE.what: The debt-to-equity ratio exceeds the 2:1 target threshold.
HIGH_LEVERAGE.fix: Verify total liabilities (2999) and total equity (3999) are correctly mapped. If the data is accurate, this is a genuine financial concern.

LOW_PROFITABILITY.what: Return on Assets (ROA) is below 1%. The cooperative is generating very little profit relative to its asset base.
LOW_PROFITABILITY.fix: Verify income accounts (4101, 4102, 4201) and expense accounts (5101–5301) are all correctly mapped and that the current year surplus (3302) is present.

MISSING_DATA.what: A critical field that is required for financial analysis is missing from the extracted data.
MISSING_DATA.fix: Check the unmapped items section at the bottom of the table. The field may have been extracted but not assigned a code. Use the dropdown to assign the correct account code.

DEFAULT.what: A data quality or financial health issue was detected.
DEFAULT.fix: Review the flagged value, check for misassigned account codes, and click Re-validate after making corrections.

cooperativeAnalytics.totalMembersTooltip: The number of members recorded in the member register, including dormant and exited members. It shows the size of the membership base. Taken from the uploaded member ledger of the approved submission. Formula: all members in the register.
cooperativeAnalytics.activeMembersTooltip: Members whose status in the register is active. A high share means an engaged membership. Taken from the uploaded member ledger of the approved submission. Formula: members with status active.
cooperativeAnalytics.dormantMembersTooltip: Members whose status in the register is dormant, meaning they are still members but no longer take part. A high share suggests members need to be re-engaged. Taken from the uploaded member ledger. Formula: members with status dormant.
cooperativeAnalytics.youthMembersTooltip: Members aged 35 or younger. It shows how well the cooperative reaches young people. Taken from the age group of each member in the uploaded member ledger. Formula: members under 18 plus members aged 18 to 35.
cooperativeAnalytics.savingsAccountsTooltip: The number of savings accounts recorded in the savings register. It shows how widely savings are used. Taken from the uploaded savings ledger of the approved submission. Formula: all savings accounts in the register.
cooperativeAnalytics.totalSavingsTooltip: The sum of every balance in the uploaded savings register. It comes from the member ledger, not from the balance sheet, so it can differ from the savings on the financial statement. Shown in USD. Formula: sum of all savings account balances.
cooperativeAnalytics.activeSaversTooltip: The number of savings accounts whose status is active. The figure counts accounts, not people, so one member with two accounts counts twice. Taken from the uploaded savings ledger. Formula: savings accounts with status active.
cooperativeAnalytics.regularSaversTooltip: The share of savings accounts that receive regular contributions, monthly or quarterly. It shows whether members save steadily. Taken from the contribution frequency in the uploaded savings ledger. Formula: accounts with monthly or quarterly contributions divided by all savings accounts, as a percentage.
cooperativeAnalytics.loanAccountsTooltip: The number of loans recorded in the loan register, with the number still active shown beneath. It shows how many members borrow. Taken from the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: all loans in the register; active means not written off.
cooperativeAnalytics.totalLoansTooltip: The outstanding balance of the loans in the uploaded loan register, without written-off loans. It comes from the member ledger, not from the balance sheet. Shown in USD. Formula: sum of balances of loans that are not written off.
cooperativeAnalytics.loansInArrearsTooltip: The number of loans whose status in the loan register is in arrears, meaning repayments are late. It differs from PAR, which measures the money value overdue in the financial statement. Taken from the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: loans with status arrears.
cooperativeAnalytics.onTimeRepaymentTooltip: The share of active loans repaid on schedule. Higher is better. Taken from the repayment regularity in the loan ledger, or from performing status when regularity is not recorded. Formula: loans repaid on time divided by active loans, as a percentage.
cooperativeAnalytics.fdAccountsTooltip: The number of fixed deposits recorded in the fixed deposit register, with the number still active shown beneath. Taken from the uploaded fixed deposit ledger. Formula: all fixed deposits in the register.
cooperativeAnalytics.totalFdBalanceTooltip: The sum of the balances of all fixed deposits in the register. It comes from the member ledger, not from the balance sheet. Shown in USD. Formula: sum of fixed deposit balances.
cooperativeAnalytics.fdPenetrationTooltip: The share of members who hold a fixed deposit. It shows how far this product reaches the membership. Taken from the fixed deposit and member ledgers, and for a network it is worked out from total members, not from an average of cooperative percentages. Formula: members with a fixed deposit divided by total members, as a percentage.
cooperativeAnalytics.rolloverRateTooltip: Of the fixed deposits that reached maturity, the share the member chose to renew. A high value shows members trust the cooperative with their money. Taken from the fixed deposit ledger. Formula: rolled over deposits divided by matured plus rolled over deposits, as a percentage.
cooperativeAnalytics.noSubmissionInfo: The charts are built from your approved submissions. Once a submission is approved for the selected period, its figures appear here.
cooperativeAnalytics.noSubmissionDesc: No submission found for your cooperative. Submit financial data to unlock analytics.
cooperativeAnalytics.regComplianceInfo: Three health checks of the cooperative: how much of its assets belongs to members, how much is held as cash and bank balances, and how much of the loan book is more than 90 days late. A gauge that cannot be computed is left out instead of showing zero. Taken from the approved financial statement. Formulas: equity divided by assets, liquid assets divided by assets, and non-performing loans divided by gross loans.
cooperativeAnalytics.savingsPortfolioInfo: Three signs of how healthy savings are: how many members save, how many accounts get regular contributions and how many accounts are active. Higher is better. Taken from the uploaded savings and member ledgers. Formulas: members with savings divided by members, accounts with monthly or quarterly contributions divided by accounts, and active accounts divided by accounts, as percentages.
cooperativeAnalytics.loanProvInfo: How much of the loan book is more than 30 days late and how much of that is covered by provisions. The uncovered part is money the cooperative could lose. Taken from the approved financial statement at the period end. Formulas: overdue amount is gross loans times PAR over 30 days; covered amount is that overdue amount times provision coverage; at risk is overdue minus covered.
cooperativeAnalytics.liquidityRiskInfo: How concentrated the fixed deposits are. If a few deposits or short terms make up most of the money, members withdrawing at once could strain the cooperative. Taken from the uploaded fixed deposit ledger. Formula: deposits that depend on a single depositor divided by all fixed deposits, as a percentage.
cooperativeAnalytics.democraticInfo: How much members take part in running the cooperative, for example by attending the Annual General Meeting. Higher means stronger member control. Taken from the attendance and voting flags in the uploaded member ledger. Formula: members who attended divided by all members, as a percentage.
cooperativeAnalytics.inclusionInfo: How much of the credit goes to women, young people and rural borrowers. It shows whether lending reaches the groups the cooperative aims to serve. Taken from the borrower flags in the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: loans to each group divided by active loans, as a percentage.
cooperativeAnalytics.loanPortfolioInfo: How the active loans split between loans repaid on time and loans in arrears, by group. It shows where repayment problems sit. Taken from the status and borrower flags in the uploaded loan ledger. Formula: loans in each group divided by active loans, as a percentage.
cooperativeAnalytics.memberDemoInfo: Who the members are: the split by gender and how many are active or dormant. It shows how balanced and engaged the membership is. Taken from the uploaded member ledger of the approved submission. Formula: members in each group divided by all members, as a percentage.
cooperativeAnalytics.dormancyLeaderboardInfo: The cooperatives with the most dormant members, meaning members who no longer take part. It shows where re-engagement efforts are needed. Taken from the member status in the uploaded member ledgers. Formula: dormant members divided by all members, as a percentage.
cooperativeAnalytics.agriResilienceInfo: How well equipped the cooperative is for farming: storage, processing, irrigation and use of shared inputs. It shows resilience to weather and market shocks. Taken from the farm cooperative ledger of the approved submission. Formula: cooperatives or farmers with each asset divided by all recorded, as a percentage.

assetEvolution.title: Asset evolution
assetEvolution.subtitle: Total assets by period
assetEvolution.info: How the total size of the cooperatives in scope changes from one reporting period to the next. Growth means the balance sheet is expanding. Taken from the questionnaire of each period and added up over the cooperatives in scope. Formula: non-current assets plus current assets.

savingsTrend.title: Savings trend
savingsTrend.subtitle: Member savings by period
savingsTrend.info: How the money members hold as savings changes over time. Rising savings mean growing member trust and more funds to lend. Taken from the questionnaire of each period and added up over the cooperatives in scope. Formula: net savings value of women plus of men.

loanPortfolio.title: Loan portfolio
loanPortfolio.subtitle: Outstanding loans by period
loanPortfolio.info: How the amount members owe on loans changes over time. Growth means more lending, which is good only if repayment stays healthy. Taken from the questionnaire of each period and added up over the cooperatives in scope. Formula: outstanding loan value of women plus of men.

parTrend.title: Portfolio at risk
parTrend.subtitle: PAR trend by period
parTrend.info: The share of the loan book that is late, by how many days. It shows whether repayment problems are growing or shrinking; lower is better. Taken from the overdue-days buckets of the questionnaire of each period, using summed amounts. Formula: balance overdue for each measure divided by gross loans, as a percentage.

liquidity.title: Liquidity to member savings
liquidity.subtitle: Maintained liquidity versus the regulatory minimum
liquidity.info: How much of members' savings could be paid back at once from cash and bank balances, compared with the 15 percent minimum. The line shows the gap: above zero is a shortfall. Taken from the questionnaire of each period. Formula: liquid assets divided by member savings, as a percentage.

financialStructure.title: Effective financial structure
financialStructure.subtitle: How assets are funded and deployed
financialStructure.info: How the cooperative's assets are put to work and how they are funded. The bars show earning assets, member savings and member shares as a share of total assets; the line on the right axis shows borrowed funds. Taken from the questionnaire of each period. Formula: each item divided by total assets, as a percentage.

profitability.title: Profitability
profitability.subtitle: Net income by period
profitability.info: Whether the cooperatives made a surplus or a loss in each period. Bars above zero are surplus. Taken from the questionnaire of each period. Formula: net income as reported, otherwise total income minus total expenditure.

institutionalCapital.title: Institutional capital to assets
institutionalCapital.subtitle: Institutional capital versus the minimum ratio
institutionalCapital.info: How much of the assets is backed by the cooperative's own reserves, compared with the 8 percent minimum. The line shows the excess or deficiency. Taken from the questionnaire of each period. Formula: retained earnings plus statutory reserves plus donations, divided by total assets, as a percentage.

marketShareAssets.title: Market share by total assets
marketShareAssets.subtitle: Share of each cooperative in consolidated assets
marketShareAssets.info: How much of the total assets in view each cooperative holds. It shows which cooperatives weigh most. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period; cooperatives that did not report assets are left out. Formula: the cooperative's total assets divided by the total assets of all cooperatives shown, as a percentage.

marketShareLoans.title: Market share by loans and advances
marketShareLoans.subtitle: Share of each cooperative in the consolidated loan book
marketShareLoans.info: How much of the total loans in view each cooperative holds. It shows which cooperatives lend the most. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period; cooperatives that did not report loans are left out. Formula: the cooperative's outstanding loans divided by the outstanding loans of all cooperatives shown, as a percentage.

demographics.title: Membership profile
demographics.subtitle: Gender and age of members
demographics.info: Who the members are: registered and active members by gender, and registered members by age band. It shows how balanced and how young the membership is. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period and added up over the cooperatives in scope. The age bands are 18 to 25, 26 to 35, 36 to 60 and over 60.

governance.title: Women in governance
governance.subtitle: Share of women in leadership bodies
governance.info: How many women sit on the board, the executive committee and the credit committee. It shows whether women take part in decisions. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: women on each body divided by all its members, as a percentage.

ranking.title: Cooperative ranking
ranking.subtitle: Key ratios per cooperative
ranking.info: The main figures of each cooperative for the selected period, side by side. A dash means the cooperative did not report the figure. Colours compare PAR over 30 days with the tolerance (green up to 5 percent, amber up to 10, red above) and liquidity and capital with their regulatory minimums of 15 and 8 percent. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period.

help.registered_members: Everyone enrolled as a member, women and men together. It shows the size of the membership base. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period and added up across the cooperatives in scope. Formula: registered women plus registered men.
help.active_members: Members who are currently active, meaning they take part in the cooperative. A value close to the registered members means an engaged base. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: active women plus active men.
help.inactive_members: Registered members who are not active. A high number suggests members have drifted away and may need to be re-engaged. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: registered members minus active members.
help.active_members_pct: The share of registered members who are active. Higher is better, because it shows how engaged the membership is. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: active members divided by registered members, as a percentage.
help.women_members_pct: The share of registered members who are women. It shows how well women are included in the membership. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: registered women divided by registered members, as a percentage.
help.youth_members_pct: The share of registered members aged 18 to 35. It shows how well the cooperative reaches young people. Taken from the age bands of the questionnaire, so it is only as complete as those bands. Formula: members aged 18 to 25 plus members aged 26 to 35, divided by registered members, as a percentage.
help.number_of_groups: The number of member groups (such as savings or credit groups) that the cooperative reports. It shows how members are organised. Entered directly in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported number of groups.
help.total_deposits: The money members hold as savings with the cooperative. It is the main source of funds for lending. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: net savings value of women plus net savings value of men.
help.deposit_accounts: The number of savings accounts held by members. It shows how widely savings are used. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: savings accounts of women plus savings accounts of men.
help.avg_savings_per_account: The typical amount saved per account. It shows how deep savings are, not only how many accounts exist. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: total member savings divided by savings accounts.
help.gross_loan_portfolio: The total amount members still owe on loans, including overdue loans, before any provisions. It is the cooperative's main earning asset. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period; if the outstanding values are missing it is estimated from the amount owed by members. Formula: outstanding loan value of women plus of men.
help.loans_outstanding_count: The number of loans that are still being repaid. It shows how many members are borrowing. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period; when it is not entered, the number of loan accounts issued is used and the figure is marked approximate. Formula: the reported number of loans outstanding.
help.avg_loan_balance: The typical balance still owed per loan. It shows the size of the loans the cooperative gives. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period; approximate when the number of loans outstanding is itself estimated. Formula: gross loan portfolio divided by loans outstanding.
help.total_disbursed_active: The original amount lent out on loans that are still active. Compared with the outstanding balance, it shows how much has already been repaid. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported total disbursed on active loans.
help.loans_awaiting_approval: The number of loan applications waiting for a decision. A long queue can point to slow approval. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported number of loans awaiting approval.
help.loans_in_arrears_count: The number of loans with at least one late payment. It shows how many borrowers are struggling, whatever the amount. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported number of loans in arrears.
help.projected_interest_earnings: A rough estimate of the interest the loan book could earn. It is approximate only, because real earnings depend on the repayment schedules. Built from the questionnaire's average interest rate, average term and interest method. Formula: gross loans times the monthly rate times the average term, halved for the share of loans on reducing balance.
help.female_borrowers_pct: The share of borrowers who are women. It shows whether women get fair access to credit. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period; when the number of women borrowers is not entered, loan accounts issued to women are used and the figure is marked approximate. Formula: women borrowers divided by loans outstanding, as a percentage.
help.total_overdrafts: The total amount of overdrafts granted to members. Overdrafts are short-term and can be risky if they are not cleared. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported total overdrafts.
help.par_gt_7_pct: The share of the loan book that is more than 7 days late. It is an early warning of repayment problems. Needs the overdue-days buckets of the Loan Quality section, otherwise it is not reported. Formula: balance overdue more than 7 days divided by gross loans, as a percentage.
help.par_gt_30_pct: Portfolio at risk over 30 days: the share of the loan book that is more than 30 days late. A high value means many loans may not be repaid, so lower is better. Uses the overdue-days buckets; if they are empty, the 31 to 365 day delinquency field is used and the figure is marked approximate. Formula: balance overdue more than 30 days divided by gross loans, as a percentage.
help.par_gt_90_pct: The share of the loan book that is more than 90 days late. These loans are unlikely to be recovered, so lower is better. Needs the overdue-days buckets of the Loan Quality section. Formula: balance overdue more than 90 days divided by gross loans, as a percentage.
help.par_30_90_pct: The share of the loan book that is between 31 and 90 days late. It shows loans that are seriously late but not yet in the worst group. Needs the overdue-days buckets of the Loan Quality section. Formula: balance overdue 31 to 90 days divided by gross loans, as a percentage.
help.par_180_360_pct: The share of the loan book that is between 181 and 360 days late. These loans are very old and most likely need to be written off. Needs the overdue-days buckets of the Loan Quality section. Formula: balance overdue 181 to 360 days divided by gross loans, as a percentage.
help.portfolio_at_risk_pct: The share of the loan book that is late by any number of days. It is the broadest measure of repayment trouble, so lower is better. Approximate when it relies on the delinquency fields instead of the overdue-days buckets. Formula: all overdue balance divided by gross loans, as a percentage.
help.value_at_risk: The money value of all loans that are late by any number of days. It shows how much of the loan book is exposed. Approximate when it relies on the delinquency fields. Formula: the balance of all overdue loans.
help.var_gt_7: The money value of loans more than 7 days late. Needs the overdue-days buckets of the Loan Quality section. Formula: balance overdue more than 7 days.
help.var_gt_30: The money value of loans more than 30 days late. It is the amount behind the portfolio at risk over 30 days. Approximate when only the 31 to 365 day delinquency field is available. Formula: balance overdue more than 30 days.
help.var_gt_90: The money value of loans more than 90 days late, the ones least likely to be recovered. Needs the overdue-days buckets of the Loan Quality section. Formula: balance overdue more than 90 days.
help.interest_in_suspense: Interest charged on loans but not counted as income because the borrower is not paying. A high amount signals weak loans. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported interest in suspense.
help.interest_payable: Interest the cooperative owes but has not yet paid, for example on member savings or borrowings. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported interest payable.
help.written_off_loans: The value of loans the cooperative has given up trying to collect and removed from its books. It shows past credit losses. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported written-off loans.
help.liquid_assets: Cash and money in the bank that can be used quickly to pay members. It shows the cooperative's ability to meet withdrawals. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: cash on hand plus cash at bank plus money in bank investments.
help.liquidity_ratio_pct: How much of members' savings the cooperative could pay back immediately from cash and bank balances. The regulatory minimum is 15 percent, so higher is safer. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: liquid assets divided by member savings, as a percentage.
help.liquidity_minimum_pct: The minimum liquidity a cooperative must keep, set by regulation at 15 percent of member savings. It is a fixed reference value, not reported by the cooperative. Formula: fixed regulatory minimum of liquid assets to member savings.
help.liquidity_gap_pct: How far the cooperative is from the 15 percent liquidity minimum. A positive value is a shortfall that needs attention; zero or negative means the minimum is met. Formula: the minimum liquidity minus the liquidity ratio, in percentage points.
help.total_assets: Everything the cooperative owns. It shows the overall size of the cooperative. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: non-current assets plus total current assets.
help.earning_asset_ratio: The share of assets that earn income, mainly loans and investments. Higher means more of the cooperative's money is put to work. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: loans plus investments, divided by total assets, as a percentage.
help.member_savings_ratio: The share of assets that is funded by member savings. A high share means the cooperative relies mostly on its members' money. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: member savings divided by total assets, as a percentage.
help.member_share_ratio: The share of assets that is funded by the shares members have bought. It shows how much members own directly. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: member share capital divided by total assets, as a percentage.
help.borrowed_funds_ratio: The share of assets that is funded by money borrowed from outside. A high share means more dependence on lenders and more risk. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: borrowed funds divided by total assets, as a percentage.
help.loans_to_savings_ratio: How much has been lent out for each unit saved. Around 100 percent or more means savings are fully lent, which leaves less cash for withdrawals. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: gross loan portfolio divided by member savings, as a percentage.
help.institutional_capital: The cooperative's own reserves built up over time, which absorb losses. It excludes the shares members bought. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: retained earnings plus statutory reserves plus donations and grants.
help.institutional_capital_ratio_pct: How much of the cooperative's assets is backed by its own reserves. The regulatory minimum is 8 percent, so higher means a stronger cushion against losses. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: institutional capital divided by total assets, as a percentage.
help.institutional_capital_minimum_pct: The minimum institutional capital a cooperative must hold, set by regulation at 8 percent of total assets. It is a fixed reference value, not reported by the cooperative. Formula: fixed regulatory minimum of institutional capital to assets.
help.institutional_capital_excess_pct: How far the institutional capital ratio is above or below the 8 percent minimum. Positive means the minimum is exceeded; negative is a deficiency that needs attention. Formula: institutional capital ratio minus the minimum, in percentage points.
help.total_equity: What is left for the members after all debts are paid. It shows the cooperative's net worth. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period; when it is not entered it is worked out from assets and liabilities and marked approximate. Formula: total equity as reported, otherwise total assets minus liabilities.
help.share_capital: The money members have paid in by buying shares. It is the members' direct stake in the cooperative. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported total share capital.
help.retained_earnings: Surpluses kept in the cooperative from past years instead of being paid out. They build the cooperative's own strength. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported retained earnings.
help.statutory_reserves: Reserves the cooperative must set aside by law or by its rules to protect against losses. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported accumulated statutory reserves.
help.total_income: All the money the cooperative earned during the year, mainly from loan interest and fees. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported current year total income.
help.total_expenditure: All the money the cooperative spent during the year to run its business. Entered in the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: the reported current year total expenditure.
help.net_income: What is left after all expenses are paid. A positive value is a surplus, a negative value is a loss. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: net income as reported, otherwise total income minus total expenditure.
help.return_on_assets_pct: How much surplus the cooperative makes for each unit of assets it holds. Higher means assets are used more profitably. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period, for the period covered and not annualised. Formula: net income divided by total assets, as a percentage.
help.operating_expense_ratio_pct: How much of each unit earned is spent on expenses. Below 100 percent the cooperative makes a surplus; lower is better. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: total expenditure divided by total income, as a percentage.
help.board_women_pct: The share of board members who are women. It shows whether women take part in the top decisions. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: women on the board divided by all board members, as a percentage.
help.executive_women_pct: The share of executive committee members who are women. It shows whether women take part in daily management. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: women on the executive divided by all executive members, as a percentage.
help.credit_committee_women_pct: The share of credit committee members who are women. It shows whether women take part in lending decisions. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: women on the credit committee divided by all its members, as a percentage.
help.agm_attendance_pct: The share of active members who came to the last Annual General Meeting. It shows how much members take part in governance. Taken from the questionnaire of the selected period. Formula: members who attended the last meeting divided by active members, as a percentage.
